library(nlmixr2lib)

library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Geers_2022_clozapine")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1177/20451253211065857>
* Open-access full text: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9066631/>

Geers and colleagues built a small therapeutic-drug-monitoring model for
clozapine with the `KinPop` module of MwPharm 3.81, using an iterative two-stage
Bayesian procedure rather than nonlinear mixed-effects modelling. The purpose is
a limited sampling strategy (LSS): one to three concentrations, combined with the
population model by Bayesian forecasting, should recover the steady-state
AUC(0-12 h) of a twice-daily regimen or the AUC(0-24 h) of a once-daily regimen
as well as a full profile would.

The structure is the simplest one the data allowed. A one-compartment model with
first-order absorption won; a lag time, a peripheral compartment and
distribution into fat tissue were each added and rejected on AIC. Only the
elimination rate constant and the per-kg volume were estimated. The absorption
rate constant could not be estimated (few samples fell in the absorption
phase), so it stayed at the literature prior of the default model (Jerling and
colleagues, 1994), and bioavailability was fixed at 1, so the volume is an
apparent `V/F`.

Concentrations came from two sample types. Venous plasma and capillary
dried-blood-spot (DBS) samples were drawn at the same times, and each DBS
whole-blood result was converted to a plasma-equivalent concentration with a
factor from the authors' earlier clinical validation of the method in the same
patients. Both were fitted as plasma, so the model has a single output, `Cc`,
the plasma clozapine concentration in ug/L.

# Population

```{r population}
str(mod()$meta$population)
```

Fifteen adults with schizophrenia (12 men, 3 women) from a Dutch community
mental-health organisation, on a stable clozapine dose for at least two weeks,
were included. All were of Western European descent, an inclusion criterion
meant to limit genetic variation in CYP1A2 expression. Mean age was 44 years and
mean body weight 90 kg; doses ranged from 75 to 800 mg/day with a mean of
287 mg/day. Ten of the 15 smoked, and eight carried co-medication that can
affect clozapine levels (fluvoxamine, omeprazole, insulin, sodium valproate);
none of these was tested as a covariate (Table 1).

To allow daytime sampling, patients on a once-daily regimen took half of their
evening dose the evening before sampling and the other half in the morning, so
every profile was collected under twice-daily dosing. Samples were taken
pre-dose and 2, 4, 6 and 8 h after the morning dose: 49 plasma and 72 DBS
concentrations in total (Table 2).

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source location |

| Elimination: `Kel = Kelm + Kelr * CLcr`, `Kelr` set to 0 | -- | Methods, Population PK model |
| Volume: per kg body weight, `V = Vd * WT` | -- | Methods ('expressed in L/kg bodyweight'); Results ('per kg body weight'); Table 3 unit 'L/kgLBMc' |

# Structural verification

## The solved profile matches its own closed form

For a one-compartment model with first-order absorption at steady state the
concentration over a dosing interval `tau` is

`C(t) = F * D * ka / (V * (ka - kel)) * (exp(-kel t) / (1 - exp(-kel tau)) - exp(-ka t) / (1 - exp(-ka tau)))`.

This chunk solves the representative patient the paper used for its Monte Carlo
simulation (male, 83 kg, 400 mg/day) on both regimens with `zeroRe()` and
compares the last interval against the closed form. Both sides use the same
typical parameters, so the difference is pure integrator error and a tight bound
is correct.

```{r closed-form}
css_closed <- function(t, dose, tau, ka, kel, v, f = 1) {
  1000 * f * dose / v * ka / (ka - kel) *
    (exp(-kel * t) / (1 - exp(-kel * tau)) - exp(-ka * t) / (1 - exp(-ka * tau)))
}

th <- c(ka = 1.37, kel = 0.0641, vd = 5.21)
wt_rep <- 83
n_days <- 14

typ_events <- function(dose, tau, id) {
  n_dose <- n_days * 24 / tau
  t_last <- (n_dose - 1) * tau
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = id, time = 0, amt = dose, ii = tau, addl = n_dose - 1, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = id, time = t_last + seq(0, tau, by = 0.25), amt = 0, ii = 0, addl = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = wt_rep, tau = tau, t_last = t_last)
}
typ_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(typ_events(200, 12, 1L), typ_events(400, 24, 2L))

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_ev, keep = c("tau", "t_last"),
  atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-12
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dose = ifelse(id == 1, 200, 400),
    tad = time - t_last,
    closed = css_closed(tad, dose, tau, th[["ka"]], th[["kel"]], th[["vd"]] * wt_rep),
    rel_err = abs(Cc - closed) / closed
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(typ) == 49L + 97L,
  # 14 days is ~20 typical half-lives, so the solve is at steady state to far
  # better than the integrator tolerance.
  max(typ$rel_err) < 1e-6
)

typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen = ifelse(id == 1, "200 mg q12h", "400 mg q24h")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Cmax (ug/L)` = max(Cc),
    `Tmax (h)` = tad[which.max(Cc)],
    `Ctrough (ug/L)` = Cc[tad == max(tad)],
    `max relative error vs closed form` = format(signif(max(rel_err), 2), scientific = TRUE)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

The typical clearance of the representative patient is
`0.0641 * 5.21 * 83 = 27.7 L/h` and the typical half-life
`log(2) / 0.0641 = 10.8 h`. At 400 mg/day the average steady-state
concentration is about 600 ug/L, inside the 350-700 ug/L trough window the
paper quotes as therapeutic.

```{r typical-plot}
ggplot(typ, aes(tad, Cc, colour = ifelse(id == 1, "200 mg q12h", "400 mg q24h"))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Clozapine plasma concentration (ug/L)",
    colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical steady-state profiles, representative patient (83 kg, 400 mg/day)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Virtual cohort

The cohort is the source population in outline: body weight drawn around the
Table 1 mean of 90 kg (SD 13 kg) and a daily dose of 300 mg, close to the
cohort mean of 287 mg/day, given either as 150 mg twice daily or 300 mg once
daily. 100 subjects per regimen.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() seeds R's RNG, which draws the covariates below, so the COHORT is
# reproducible. It does not seed rxode2's eta sampler, whose streams are
# partitioned per solver thread, so every assertion downstream on an
# eta-driven quantity is written to hold for any draw.
set.seed(20220101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20220101)
n_per_arm <- 100L

make_arm <- function(n, dose, tau, id_offset, regimen) {
  wt <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 90, 13), 55), 130)
  n_dose <- n_days * 24 / tau
  t_last <- (n_dose - 1) * tau
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose, ii = tau, addl = n_dose - 1,
    evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = t_last + seq(0, tau, by = 0.25)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, ii = 0, addl = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::left_join(data.frame(id = ids, WT = wt), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = regimen, tau = tau, t_last = t_last, dose = dose) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_arm(n_per_arm, 150, 12, 0L, "150 mg q12h"),
  make_arm(n_per_arm, 300, 24, n_per_arm, "300 mg q24h")
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

events |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, regimen, WT) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), `median WT (kg)` = median(WT), `min WT` = min(WT), `max WT` = max(WT)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events = events,
  keep = c("regimen", "tau", "t_last", "dose", "WT")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_last)
```

```{r iiv-recovery}
# The individual parameters ride along in the output; their spread is a check
# that the variances were carried onto the right parameters.
indiv <- sim |> dplyr::distinct(id, regimen, ka, kel, vd, cl, vc)
stopifnot(nrow(indiv) == 2L * n_per_arm)
iiv <- data.frame(
  parameter = c("ka", "kel", "vd"),
  published_mean = c(1.37, 0.0641, 5.21),
  published_cv_pct = 100 * c(0.68 / 1.37, 0.0365 / 0.0641, 3.82 / 5.21),
  simulated_median = c(median(indiv$ka), median(indiv$kel), median(indiv$vd)),
  simulated_cv_pct = 100 * c(sd(indiv$ka) / mean(indiv$ka), sd(indiv$kel) / mean(indiv$kel), sd(indiv$vd) / mean(indiv$vd))
)
knitr::kable(iiv, digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  # Medians of a 200-subject log-normal draw: generous multiplicative bounds.
  all(abs(log(iiv$simulated_median / iiv$published_mean)) < log(1.35))
)
```

## Simulated concentration-time profiles

Figure 1 of the paper shows the measured concentrations, which span roughly
30-900 ug/L across the 2-8 h sampling window for the 15 patients and their
range of doses. The shaded band below is the 5th-95th percentile of the
simulated individual concentrations for a 150 mg twice-daily regimen, with the
residual error (`sim`) shown as points for a sample of subjects.

```{r vpc}
vpc <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(tad, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(
    data = sim |> dplyr::filter(id %% 10 == 0, tad %in% c(0, 2, 4, 6, 8)),
    aes(tad, sim), inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.5, size = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Clozapine plasma concentration (ug/L)",
    title = "Steady-state profiles at 300 mg/day: median and 90% interval"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over the final dosing interval of each regimen. The
observation grid places records at both interval endpoints.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, time, Cc, regimen)

# Guarantee a time = 0 record per subject; pre-dose concentration is 0.
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, regimen) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, regimen, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

# Dose records expanded from addl so PKNCA sees every dose.
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, amt, ii, addl, regimen) |>
  tidyr::uncount(addl + 1L, .id = "k") |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = (k - 1) * ii) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  as.data.frame(sim_nca), Cc ~ time | regimen + id,
  concu = "ug/L", timeu = "h"
)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  as.data.frame(dose_df), amt ~ time | regimen + id,
  doseu = "mg", route = "extravascular"
)

windows <- events |> dplyr::distinct(regimen, tau, t_last)
intervals <- data.frame(
  regimen = windows$regimen,
  start = windows$t_last,
  end = windows$t_last + windows$tau,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_par <- c("cmax", "tmax", "cmin", "auclast", "cav")
nca_raw <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% nca_par)
stopifnot(
  nrow(dplyr::count(nca_raw, regimen, id, PPTESTCD) |> dplyr::filter(n > 1L)) == 0L
)

nca_tbl <- nca_raw |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
stopifnot(
  nrow(nca_tbl) == 2L * n_per_arm,
  all(vapply(nca_tbl[nca_par], is.numeric, logical(1))),
  !anyNA(nca_tbl$auclast)
)

nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(nca_par), ~ median(.x)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Regimen = regimen, `Cmax (ug/L)` = cmax, `Tmax (h)` = tmax,
    `Cmin (ug/L)` = cmin, `AUC0-tau (ug*h/L)` = auclast, `Cav (ug/L)` = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median steady-state NCA per regimen (300 mg/day).")
```

At steady state a linear model must satisfy `CL * AUC(0-tau) = F * Dose`,
evaluated per subject against that subject's own clearance. Both sides use the
same drawn parameters; the gap is trapezoidal error on a 0.25 h grid plus, for a
handful of subjects with very slow elimination, an incomplete approach to steady
state after 14 days. The centre is therefore held tightly and the tail by a
robust quantile.

```{r gate-ss-mass-balance}
mb <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::left_join(indiv |> dplyr::select(id, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::left_join(events |> dplyr::distinct(id, dose), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_expected = 1000 * dose / cl, # ug*h/L, F = 1
    pct_diff = 100 * (auclast - auc_expected) / auc_expected
  )
stopifnot(
  nrow(mb) == 2L * n_per_arm,
  abs(median(mb$pct_diff)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(mb$pct_diff), 0.9) < 3
)
mb |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `median % diff` = median(pct_diff),
    `90th pct |% diff|` = quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Simulated AUC0-tau versus F * Dose / CL.")
```

## Comparison against published NCA

The paper reports no NCA summary (Cmax, Tmax, AUC or half-life) for its
cohort, so there is no published NCA table to compare against. The quantitative
results it does report are the limited-sampling performance statistics of
Table 4, which are reproduced in the next section. Figure 2 plots individual
full-curve against two-point AUC(0-12 h) values on axes labelled `mg*h/L` that
run from about 25 to 325; with the measured concentrations of Figure 1 at
30-900 ug/L, a 12 h AUC can be at most about 11 mg*h/L, so the Figure 2 axis
unit cannot be taken at face value and that figure is not used as a numeric
target.

# Reproducing the limited sampling strategy (Table 4)

The paper's LSS was derived by Monte Carlo simulation of 1000 virtual patients
with the characteristics of the representative patient (83 kg, 400 mg/day),
followed by Bayesian (maximum a posteriori, MAP) estimation of each patient's
AUC from a subset of sampling times, compared with that patient's true AUC by
the root mean squared prediction error (RMSE, %), the mean prediction error
(MPE, %) and r^2. A scheme was "sufficiently predictive" when r^2 > 0.95,
RMSE < 15% and MPE < 5%.

The replication below follows that design in plain R so it is independent of
the rxode2 random-number stream: 200 virtual patients drawn from the model's
IIV (including the Ka prior), steady-state concentrations from the closed form
validated above, assay error `SD = 10 + 0.1 C`, and MAP estimation of `Kel` and
`Vd` with `Ka` held at its population value (it was not Bayesian-estimated in
the paper). The true AUC is `F * Dose / CL`. The twice-daily interval uses
200 mg every 12 h and the once-daily interval 400 mg every 24 h; the
percentage statistics do not depend on dose.

```{r lss}
om <- c(ka = 0.220230, kel = 0.280840, vd = 0.430216)

neg_log_post <- function(eta, obs, times, dose, tau, wt) {
  pred <- css_closed(times, dose, tau, th[["ka"]], th[["kel"]] * exp(eta[1]), th[["vd"]] * exp(eta[2]) * wt)
  sdv <- 10 + 0.1 * pred
  sum(((obs - pred) / sdv)^2 + 2 * log(sdv)) / 2 + sum(eta^2 / om[c("kel", "vd")]) / 2
}

schemes <- data.frame(
  interval = c(rep("0-12", 4), rep("0-24", 4)),
  samples = c("12", "4", "2, 6", "2, 6, 8", "24", "7", "4, 11", "4, 10, 11"),
  pub_rmse = c(23.35, 13.04, 9.06, 6.87, 34.87, 13.58, 7.67, 5.76),
  pub_r2 = c(0.9710, 0.9905, 0.9954, 0.9974, 0.9374, 0.9912, 0.9971, 0.9984),
  pub_mpe = c(5.81, 0.56, -0.20, -0.18, 1.95, -3.02, -0.36, -0.34),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

set.seed(2022)
n_mc <- 200L
eta_mc <- matrix(rnorm(3 * n_mc), ncol = 3) %*% diag(sqrt(om))
ka_i <- th[["ka"]] * exp(eta_mc[, 1])
kel_i <- th[["kel"]] * exp(eta_mc[, 2])
v_i <- th[["vd"]] * exp(eta_mc[, 3]) * wt_rep

lss_one <- function(interval, samples) {
  tau <- if (interval == "0-12") 12 else 24
  dose <- if (interval == "0-12") 200 else 400
  times <- as.numeric(strsplit(samples, ",")[[1]])
  auc_true <- dose / (kel_i * v_i)
  auc_est <- vapply(seq_len(n_mc), function(i) {
    pred <- css_closed(times, dose, tau, ka_i[i], kel_i[i], v_i[i])
    obs <- pred + rnorm(length(pred)) * (10 + 0.1 * pred)
    fit <- optim(c(0, 0), neg_log_post, obs = obs, times = times, dose = dose, tau = tau, wt = wt_rep)
    dose / (th[["kel"]] * exp(fit$par[1]) * th[["vd"]] * exp(fit$par[2]) * wt_rep)
  }, numeric(1))
  pe <- (auc_est - auc_true) / auc_true
  data.frame(
    sim_rmse = 100 * sqrt(mean(pe^2)),
    sim_r2 = cor(auc_est, auc_true)^2,
    sim_mpe = 100 * mean(pe)
  )
}

lss <- dplyr::bind_cols(
  schemes,
  dplyr::bind_rows(Map(lss_one, schemes$interval, schemes$samples))
)

lss |>
  dplyr::select(interval, samples, pub_rmse, sim_rmse, pub_r2, sim_r2, pub_mpe, sim_mpe) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `AUC interval (h)` = interval, `Sampling times (h)` = samples,
    `RMSE % (paper)` = pub_rmse, `RMSE % (replication)` = sim_rmse,
    `r2 (paper)` = pub_r2, `r2 (replication)` = sim_r2,
    `MPE % (paper)` = pub_mpe, `MPE % (replication)` = sim_mpe
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 4, 4, 2, 2), caption = "Replicates Table 4 of Geers 2022.")
```

```{r lss-gate}
multi <- lss |> dplyr::filter(grepl(",", samples))
stopifnot(
  # The paper's own acceptance criteria for every two- and three-point scheme,
  # which the replication meets with several points of headroom.
  all(multi$sim_rmse < 15),
  all(multi$sim_r2 > 0.95),
  all(abs(multi$sim_mpe) < 5),
  # Each multi-point RMSE lands within a factor of 1.5 of the published one.
  all(abs(log(multi$sim_rmse / multi$pub_rmse)) < log(1.5))
)
```

The replication reproduces the paper's conclusion: the recommended two-point
schemes (2 and 6 h for AUC(0-12 h); 4 and 11 h for AUC(0-24 h)) and the
three-point schemes meet all three criteria, with RMSE values close to the
published ones, and a single trough sample is the weakest predictor. The
once-daily trough row in Table 4 is labelled "12 (trough level)"; it is
simulated here at 24 h, the trough of a once-daily interval, and lands close
to the published RMSE of 34.87% and r^2 of 0.9374 (a 12 h sample in a 24 h
interval gives a much smaller error, so the published row cannot be a 12 h
sample). Exact agreement is not expected: the paper used 1000 MwPharm Monte
Carlo patients and its own MAP implementation.

# Assumptions and deviations

## Volume normaliser: body weight

Table 3 prints the unit of `Vd/F` as `L/kgLBMc`, the MwPharm fat-corrected lean
body mass `LBMc = LBM + (WT - LBM) * fd`. The prose states twice that the volume
is per kg body weight ("for simplicity clozapine volume of distribution is
expressed in L/kg bodyweight", Methods; "distribution volume per kg body weight
(Vd)", Results), and the paper reports that adding the "percentage of
distribution into fatty tissue" (the `fd` factor) did not improve the model.
The two statements agree when `fd = 1`, for which `LBMc = WT`. The model
therefore uses `V = Vd * WT`. The choice has little effect for the paper's
representative patient (83 kg, 188 cm, whose MwPharm lean body mass
`50 + 0.9 * (188 - 152) = 82.4 kg` is almost his weight). For the cohort-mean
man (90 kg, 1.81 m, lean body mass 76 kg) the alternative `fd = 0` reading
(volume per kg lean body mass) would give a volume about 15% smaller, and the
gap grows for heavier, shorter patients.

## Interpretation of the reported "mean +/- SD" pairs

MwPharm's iterative two-stage Bayesian output is a population mean with an
interindividual SD on the natural scale. With parameters assumed log-normal,
the mean is carried as the typical value (`exp(theta)`) and the SD converted
to a log-scale variance via `omega^2 = log(1 + (SD / mean)^2)`, as for the
other MwPharm-built model in this library (Daskapan 2019, darunavir). If the
printed value were instead the arithmetic mean of a log-normal, the median
would be lower by the factor `sqrt(1 + CV^2)` (about 13% for `Kel` and 19% for
`Vd`). No covariance between parameters is reported, so the IIV block is
diagonal.

## Absorption IIV kept as a fixed prior

The absorption rate constant was not Bayesian-estimated; Table 3 lists it with
its literature prior SD, `1.37 +/- 0.68 (fixed)`. The SD is carried as a fixed
variance on `etalka` so that the full prior the paper used in Bayesian
forecasting is preserved. Set it to zero to reproduce a typical-absorption
model.

## Renal elimination omitted

The published elimination model is `Kel = Kelm + Kelr * CLcr` with `Kelr` set to
zero because clozapine is not renally excreted unchanged. With `Kelr = 0` the
creatinine-clearance term is identically zero, so it is not carried and the
model needs no creatinine-clearance column.

## DBS conversion

DBS concentrations were converted to plasma-equivalent values before fitting
with a conversion factor from the authors' earlier validation study, which is
not restated in this paper. The model predicts plasma concentration; to compare
with raw DBS whole-blood measurements the same conversion must be applied.

## Covariates not modelled

Smoking, co-medication (notably the CYP1A2 inhibitor fluvoxamine in 3 of 15
patients), sex and age were recorded but not tested as covariates; the paper
notes their effect is absorbed into the residual and interindividual
variability. The model should not be used to predict the effect of starting or
stopping smoking or of interacting drugs.

## Once-daily applicability

All profiles were collected on a twice-daily regimen (once-daily users split
their dose for the sampling day), so the once-daily AUC(0-24 h) strategy rests
on simulation only, as the paper acknowledges.
